h2: Visual testing in Seattle: building steel, ferries, refineries and remote access
html:
Visual testing in Seattle: building steel, ferries, refineries and remote access

Visual testing in Seattle covers structural steel welds on construction projects, ferry and shipyard structure, refinery equipment inspected under API 510, 570 and 653 programs, and remote visual work inside places people cannot easily reach. Atlantis is a Houston-based company. It sends VT crews to Puget Sound sites, writes the acceptance criteria into the procedure, and has the procedure reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III.

Construction and special inspection. On permitted building work in Seattle, the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections uses the Seattle Building Code, Chapter 17, to decide which items need special inspection. The project owner, not the contractor, nominates and pays the special inspection agency. Its structural inspectors must be certified by the Washington Association of Building Officials. A fabricator's own weld VT under AWS D1.1 is a separate role from that special inspection. Before a quote, Atlantis confirms which role the job is for, because a report written for one role cannot stand in for the other.

Ferries and shipyards. Washington State Ferries keeps its fleet running from the Eagle Harbor Maintenance Facility on Bainbridge Island. The facility has ten shops, including a weld shop, though some repairs and inspections still need a dry dock. Vigor's Harbor Island yard and Puget Sound Naval Shipyard in Bremerton carry heavier repair. In all three, close visual examination comes first: weld profile, cracking at bracket toes, coating breakdown and pitting in tanks. That visual survey decides where gauging and MT are spent. Hull and tank access often depends on staging or rope access, and Atlantis can supply IRATA rope-access technicians where scaffolding is not practical.

Refineries and process plants. At the Cherry Point, Ferndale, Anacortes and Tacoma refineries, external and internal visual inspection is the base of each API 510, 570 and 653 program. Typical findings are damaged insulation jacketing, failed paint at pipe supports, tank shell and roof condition, and nozzle and flange leaks. In Washington, the Department of Labor & Industries sets pressure vessel inspection intervals in WAC 296-104-100, and owner-user programs may adopt API 510 intervals. Atlantis does the visual examination and documents it for the owner's inspector. It does not sign as an API inspector.

Remote visual. Borescopes and video probes reach exchanger channels, small-bore piping and closed structure without dismantling. Drone or rope access covers stacks, flare structures and tank shells. Each image is tied to a location, so the record works as evidence and not just as a picture.

  • AWS D1.1 weld profile, undercut and porosity checks before volumetric NDT
  • Ferry and ship structure: close-up survey before gauging plans are set
  • Tank shells, roofs and appurtenances under API 653 external inspection
  • Remote visual inside exchangers, piping and enclosed spaces

Where to go. The national service is on visual testing. Seattle weld scopes are on weld inspection in Seattle, and storage tanks on tank inspection in Seattle. Construction work is covered on construction NDT in Seattle. To learn VT, see visual testing training or practice on the VT simulator. To describe a Puget Sound visual scope, use the Seattle VT enquiry.
